title: World Bank RCT in Benin City: six weeks of Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) English tutoring in nine public schools raises assessment scores 0.31 SD
summary: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125: teacher-guided after-school Copilot (GPT-4) sessions, June-July 2024, Benin City; 0.31 SD overall, 0.23 SD in English; 657 treated, 671 control.
account: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025), by De Simone, Tiberti, Barron Rodriguez, Manolio, Mosuro and Dikoru, evaluates a six-week after-school programme run between June and July 2024 in nine public schools in Benin City, Nigeria, chosen for their computer labs. First-year senior secondary students, typically 15 years old, who expressed interest were randomised: 657 to treatment and 671 to control, of whom 422 and 337 completed the final assessment. Treated students attended up to two 90-minute sessions a week (twelve in total) in which they used Microsoft Copilot, powered by GPT-4 at the time, as a virtual English tutor in curriculum-aligned activities guided by teachers. The paper reports a 0.31 standard deviation improvement on an assessment covering English, AI knowledge and digital skills, 0.23 SD on English, gains equated to 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling, and larger effects for female students and those with higher initial performance. The World Bank blog of 9 January 2025 describes the gain as about 0.3 SD. The date observed is the first day of the programme's first month, used as a placeholder; the paper gives months, not days.
purpose: Copilot was used as a virtual tutor to improve English learning outcomes; the measured gain is that purpose.
system: Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) used as a virtual English tutor in teacher-guided after-school computer-lab sessions
model_version: GPT-4 (Microsoft Copilot, per the working paper)
deployer: Nine public secondary schools in Benin City with the World Bank study team; sessions guided by teachers
taxonomy_note: Cohort-level RCT, so general benefit with null depths. The abstract gives 0.23 SD for English while the paper's results section gives 0.24 sigma for the English section; the abstract figure is used. This study already appears as an echo on AIBD-0039 but has no record of its own in the existing headlines.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an individually attributable event: treated students scored 0.31 SD higher overall and 0.23 SD higher in English after six weeks (working paper abstract).
General benefit without an event: the schools and the study team gained a cost-effectiveness estimate of 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling (working paper abstract).

ai_role.statement: Copilot was the tutor inside teacher-guided sessions, so the estimate is of the whole after-school programme (twelve 90-minute sessions); the LLM's contribution is not isolated from teacher guidance and extra instructional time.
